fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS ~$11.3 at Sep-2027 x 21x = $237, weight 0.5), DCF (~$198, weight 0.3) and EV/sales (FY28 revenue ~$3.7B x 11x + ~$1.7B net cash = ~$212, weight 0.2) on ~200M diluted shares incl. DustPhotonics earn-out shares; blended ~$220.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS as of Sep-2027 ~$11.3 (blend of FY28 ~$9.4, a small haircut to $9.63 consensus for optical-mix margin, and FY29 ~$12.3); 21x multiple (was 22x: trimmed for peer multiple compression per Mizuho's $290->$245 cut, a 43%-of-revenue direct customer, and Marvell pricing 1.6T AEC silicon below Credo).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF after SBC burden: FY28 ~$1.35B (revenue ~$3.7B, ~48% non-GAAP net margin, less ~$0.4B SBC and a working-capital drag given Q1 OCF of only $90M on $236M non-GAAP NI) growing 25%/yr to FY32; WACC 11%; terminal growth 4%; EV ~$38.0B + ~$1.7B net cash by Sep-2027; / 200M shares.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: FY28 (May-2028) revenue ~$3.7B (+48% on ~$2.5B FY27, between my old +35% and the supervisor's consensus-implied +55%); 11x EV/sales (vs ~16x FY27 today) as growth decelerates; + ~$1.7B net cash by Sep-2027 (from $764M cash+investments post-DustPhotonics); / 200M shares.

bear.story: AI capex digestion, or Amazon (the 43% direct customer; Trn3 ramp) dual-sources 1.6T AECs to cheaper Marvell-based cables; H2 FY27 ramp slips on supply or inventory digestion (inventory already $313M); gross margin erodes on optical mix; FY28 EPS ~$7.5 x ~14.5x.

base.story: FY27 delivers ~$2.5B (+85-90%) with the guided ~23% q/q H2 ramp and >$600M optical; FY28 grows ~45-50% to ~$3.7B as management's 'outsized growth again' plays out (ALC and OmniConnect start contributing, Trn3/GB300/MSFT/META ramps); non-GAAP EPS ~$9.4 FY28 / ~$11.3 NTM at ~21x.

bull.story: FY28 lands at or above consensus-implied ~$3.9B+, optical (ZeroFlap, DustPhotonics SiPho, DSPs) scales past $1B run-rate, 3-4 customers >10% ease concentration, Credo holds 1.6T AEC share; FY28 EPS $11+ and NTM ~$13.5 at ~27x.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$125 the stock would be ~17% below the verified $150.09 capitulation close of 2026-09-14 (a sentiment-only selloff after a beat-and-raise) and ~13x FY28 consensus EPS of ~$9.6 for a company guiding >85% growth. Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break: a lost/paused or dual-sourced top customer program (e.g. Amazon Trn3 moving 1.6T AECs to Marvell-based cables), a guide-down showing the H2 FY27 optical/AEC ramp failed, or a hyperscaler capex cut, rather than ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. Core facts unchanged and re-verified: Q1 FY27 revenue $479M (+115% y/y), non-GAAP NI $236M, Q2 guide $525-535M, FY27 growth >85% with >$600M optical, FY28 consensus EPS ~$9.63, post-print low close $150.09 then +41% in 9 sessions to $210.97, ~22x FY28 consensus. The supervisor correctly flagged that my +35% FY28 revenue path (~$3.4B) was inconsistent with using near-consensus EPS; consensus EPS at ~49% net margin implies ~$3.8-3.9B, and management said it expects 'outsized growth again' in FY28. I accept most of that but not all: I move to ~$3.7B (+48%), keeping a margin/haircut for optical-mix dilution and the risk that FY28 is carried by one or two customers. I also fixed my own inconsistency on net cash (EV/sales leg used $0.8-1.0B, DCF $1.8B) to a single ~$1.7B, reflecting $764M post-deal cash and weak Q1 OCF ($90M) from the inventory build to $313M. Offsetting these, new evidence is mildly negative for the multiple: Mizuho cut its target to $245 from $290 on lower peer multiples (while keeping positive Trn3/GB300 channel checks), the direct-customer concentration is 43% (57% of receivables), and Marvell is reportedly ahead and cheaper on 1.6T AEC retimers; so I trim the P/E multiple from 22x to 21x. Net: P/E 240->237, DCF 192->198, EV/sales 195->212, blended 217->220. Scenario mean ~$238 (bear 108/25%, base 240/50%, bull 365/25%), median ~$224. Dispersion unchanged: lognormal sigma ~0.66 (below 96% realized vol, which is inflated by the earnings crash and rebound, far above the 25-35% large-cap base rate), left tail kept fat because the concentration and competition findings make a customer-loss path at least as likely as I thought, far right trimmed slightly vs pure lognormal. The ladder shifts up ~0.5-1 point in the middle only; P(>= $211) 0.54, P(< $127) ~21%, P(>= $422) ~14.5%. I did not copy the supervisor's ladder; it happens to land close because the corrections roughly offset. Round 2 used 4 additional searches; no option data or priors consulted.
